push_headlines: Asia rallied on a tech rebound: the Nikkei 225 +2.87% to 60,459.58, the Hang Seng +0.44%.
Oil kept sliding on US-Iran deal hopes: Brent $91.49 (-1.17%), WTI $86.04 (-0.93%).
A hotter-than-expected US CPI report lifted Treasury yields and December rate-hike bets.
on_notice: Rate-hike pricing after the hot US CPI report is the main overnight risk for index futures.
US-Iran talks: Brent briefly dipped below $90.00 for the first time since August, so any headline on the talks can move oil sharply.
Brazil's Copom minutes and the real near 5.51 per dollar, its weakest in at least six months, keep Latin America on watch.

asia.headline: Asia rallied as AI and chip stocks rebounded and oil fell.
asia.detail: Japan's Nikkei 225 +2.87% to 60,459.58. South Korea's Kospi led the region with a gain of more than 4%, closing at 5,239.13. The rally followed a tech rebound on Wall Street and a further drop in oil.

china.headline: Hong Kong edged higher on HSBC and chip stocks; no verified Shanghai close was found.
china.detail: The Hang Seng +0.44% to 24,557.04, led by HSBC and chip names. Searches returned no citable same-day Shanghai Composite close, so no mainland level is quoted here.

europe.headline: Europe closed mostly higher on lower oil, but the hot US CPI report trimmed gains.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 closed near 658.32, within two points of its August record. Germany's DAX +0.31% to 26,347.45 after US inflation data erased most of its earlier gain, the FTSE 100 -0.29% to 10,751.59, Spain's IBEX 35 +0.98% to 19,936.40 and Italy's FTSE MIB +0.69% to 51,755.08.

latam.headline: No Tuesday close was found; Brazil's stocks came in off a strong Monday, with the real weak.
latam.detail: On Monday the Ibovespa +2.22% to 172,236, its second straight gain, but it remains 17.6% below its October high. The real ended near 5.51 per dollar, its weakest in at least six months, ahead of Tuesday's Copom minutes.

mideast.headline: Oil fell again as US-Iran deal hopes grew; Brent briefly dipped below $90.00.
mideast.detail: Brent settled at $91.49 (-1.17%) and WTI at $86.04 (-0.93%). Brent touched a session low of $89.16, its first trade below $90.00 since August, after President Trump signaled restraint on Iran while talks progress.
